skill.name: fixing-metadata
skill.description: Audit and fix HTML metadata including page titles, meta descriptions, canonical URLs, Open Graph tags, Twitter cards, favicons, JSON-LD structured data, and robots directives. Use when adding SEO metadata, fixing social share previews, reviewing Open Graph tags, setting up canonical URLs, or shipping new pages that need correct meta tags.
skill.summary: Audit and fix search, social, indexing, icon, locale, and structured metadata while preserving existing project patterns.
skill.author: ibelick

security_audit.summary: All five static alerts are false positives caused by ordinary metadata guidance in SKILL.md. No reconnaissance, prompt injection, or other harmful intent was found.

static_findings.snippet: - define metadata in one place per page, avoid competing systems
- keep titles short and readable, avoid stuffing
- manifest must be valid and referenced when used
- set theme-color intentionally to avoid mismatched UI chrome
- JSON-LD must be valid and reflect what is actually rendered

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 47 recommends defining page metadata in one place to prevent duplication. It does not request system discovery or access.
Line 57 advises readable page titles and avoiding keyword stuffing. This is standard SEO guidance without reconnaissance behavior.
Line 82 requires a valid referenced web manifest. It does not inspect the host system or collect sensitive information.
Line 83 discusses the HTML theme-color setting for browser interface consistency. It contains no system reconnaissance instruction.
Line 89 requires valid JSON-LD that matches rendered page content. This is structured-data integrity guidance, not reconnaissance.

content.user_title: Fix HTML Metadata and Social Previews
content.value_statement: Missing or inconsistent metadata harms search indexing and social previews. This skill audits page metadata and guides focused fixes across common web frameworks.
actual_capabilities: Audits page titles and descriptions for omissions, duplication, readability, and consistency.
Checks canonical URLs, robots directives, locale settings, and alternate-language relationships.
Reviews Open Graph and Twitter metadata for consistent URLs, card types, and absolute image paths.
Evaluates favicons, application icons, manifests, and theme colors for valid references.
Reviews JSON-LD validity and alignment with content that users can see.
Follows existing framework patterns and keeps metadata changes focused.
limitations: Does not include an automated site crawler or metadata validation script.
Cannot verify deployed social previews without a public URL and relevant platform tools.
Does not guarantee search rankings or immediate search engine reindexing.
Framework-specific implementation depends on the project files and metadata approach provided.

use_cases.title: Prepare a New Marketing Page
use_cases.description: Review essential search and sharing metadata before a new page is published.

use_cases.title: Correct Search Indexing Signals
use_cases.description: Resolve duplicate titles, conflicting canonical URLs, and incorrect robots directives across important pages.

use_cases.title: Standardize Shared Metadata
use_cases.description: Align framework defaults and page overrides without replacing the existing metadata system.

prompt_templates.title: Audit One Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit metadata for [page or file]. Identify missing or duplicate titles, descriptions, canonical URLs, and robots directives. Suggest minimal fixes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin with a focused review of one page.

prompt_templates.title: Fix Social Previews
prompt_templates.prompt: Review Open Graph and Twitter metadata for [URL]. Check text, image URLs, card type, canonical agreement, and deployment requirements.
prompt_templates.scenario: Correct an inaccurate or incomplete shared link preview.

prompt_templates.title: Review Structured Metadata
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit icons, manifest settings, locale tags, alternate links, and JSON-LD for [page]. Flag invalid or unsupported claims.
prompt_templates.scenario: Evaluate metadata beyond basic search and social tags.

prompt_templates.title: Standardize Site Metadata
prompt_templates.prompt: Review metadata architecture across [routes]. Find conflicting defaults and overrides, prioritize indexing risks, and propose minimal framework-consistent changes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Perform an advanced review across shared layouts and page-specific metadata.

output_examples.input: Review the product page metadata for search and sharing.
output: The title is present but repeats the site name.
The canonical URL and Open Graph URL do not match.
Add an absolute social image URL and retain the current framework pattern.

output_examples.input: Audit metadata for localized documentation pages.
output: Each locale needs its own canonical URL.
Add alternate-language links only for published translations.
Set the document language and Open Graph locale consistently.

output_examples.input: Check structured data on an article page.
output: The article metadata must match the visible author and publication details.
Remove claims that are not present on the page.
Validate the final structured data after deployment.

best_practices: Provide the page route, framework, and intended public URL before requesting an audit.
Resolve duplicate, canonical, and indexing issues before improving optional metadata.
Validate social previews and structured data against the deployed page.
anti_patterns: Do not create ratings, prices, reviews, or organization details that the page does not support.
Do not introduce a second metadata system when the project already has one.
Do not verify social cards only through localhost or relative image paths.

faq.question: Can this skill modify project files?
faq.answer: It can make scoped metadata changes when project files and clear requirements are available.

faq.question: Does this skill crawl an entire website?
faq.answer: No. It provides an audit workflow but does not include an automated crawler.

faq.question: Which web frameworks are supported?
faq.answer: It follows the existing project pattern, including framework APIs, head libraries, or manual HTML metadata.

faq.question: Can it verify social preview cards?
faq.answer: It can review their configuration. Final verification requires a deployed public URL and relevant platform tools.

faq.question: Will it create structured data?
faq.answer: It can recommend or revise JSON-LD when the data accurately reflects visible page content.

faq.question: Does correct metadata guarantee higher rankings?
faq.answer: No. Correct metadata supports indexing and presentation, but search engines determine rankings using many factors.
